scope: Design the governance track for a GitHub-hosted repository-native agent operating system: deterministic risk classification, human intervention, ownership, rulesets, guarded auto-merge, exceptions, production approval, least-privilege identities, security evidence, audit, and reconciliation. It covers issue/spec approval through merge and production promotion. It does not claim that GitHub configuration alone proves semantic safety.

The trust boundary is explicit: agents may propose code and policy changes, but they never approve their own plan, review, exception, ruleset/CODEOWNERS/CI change, evaluator or production release. Desired policy may live in Git; effective GitHub rulesets, environments, app grants, and Projects are remote state and must be independently reconciled and audited.
current_capabilities: GitHub repository/organization rulesets can target branches/tags, layer multiple applicable rules, expose rule insights, support bypass actors and enforcement states, and are manageable by REST; unlike legacy branch protection where only one matching rule applies, layered rulesets can express a risk floor ([S1](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets), [S2](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets), [S3](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules), [S17](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/orgs/rules)). Repository rules include required PRs/reviews, status checks, signed commits, linear history, merge queue, deployments, code scanning, file/path/size and workflow restrictions, subject to plan/repository availability ([S2](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets)).

CODEOWNERS is a path-to-owner routing file in `.github/`, repository root, or `docs/`; the first file in that order is used. Required code-owner review is enforcement only when a protected rule/ruleset requires it. Owners need write access, fork PR ownership is evaluated from the base branch, and the file has syntax/size limitations ([S4](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners)). Therefore CODEOWNERS is not a general separation-of-duties engine.

Protected branches/rulesets can require approvals, dismiss stale approvals, require approval of the most recent reviewable push, resolve conversations, require named checks from an expected GitHub App, restrict pushes, require deployments and a merge queue ([S5](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches)). GitHub auto-merge merely waits for branch-protection requirements and must be enabled by an authorized actor; the GraphQL mutation takes the PR ID and merge method ([S8](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/automatically-merging-a-pull-request), [S9](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#enablepullrequestautomerge)).

Merge queue builds a temporary merge group against current base and queued changes. GitHub Actions workflows that supply required checks must subscribe to `merge_group`; a workflow listening only to `pull_request` can leave the queued check missing ([S6](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue), [S7](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/events-that-trigger-workflows#merge_group)).

GitHub environments can restrict deployment branches/tags, hold environment secrets until protection rules pass, use required reviewers and prevent self-review; however only one listed reviewer needs approve, so two-person release approval needs a custom protection rule/workflow or an external release controller ([S10](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/manage-environments), [S11](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/review-deployments), [S28](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/deployments/environments)). Availability and bypass behavior vary by plan and repository visibility.

Actions supports job/workflow `permissions` for `GITHUB_TOKEN`, OIDC federation, environments and artifact attestations. GitHub warns that compromised third-party Actions and unsafe triggers can expose tokens/secrets; pin third-party actions to a full commit SHA and avoid privileged execution of fork-controlled code ([S12](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication), [S13](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions), [S14](https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/), [S26](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-hardening-your-deployments/about-security-hardening-with-openid-connect)).

Organization/enterprise audit logs and APIs record administrative and repository activity and enterprise streaming can export events, but coverage, fields and retention differ by plan/event and are not an append-only application ledger ([S16](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/keeping-your-organization-secure/managing-security-settings-for-your-organization/managing-the-audit-log-for-your-organization), [S27](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/admin/monitoring-activity-in-your-enterprise/reviewing-audit-logs-for-your-enterprise/streaming-the-audit-log-for-your-enterprise)).
representative_systems: GitHub rulesets + CODEOWNERS + merge queue are the repository merge enforcement plane; GitHub Actions is the independent evidence runner; GitHub environments/deployments are the production gate; a GitHub App is the narrow automation identity; organization/enterprise audit log is a secondary audit source.

GitHub ProjectV2 is useful for operator views, not the authoritative policy state. Its GraphQL objects use node IDs and field/item mutations ([S18](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/objects#projectv2)); the REST Projects API is for classic Projects and is closed in favor of the newer Projects experience ([S29](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/projects)). A controller must resolve symbolic manifest names to live GraphQL IDs and reconcile drift rather than pretending YAML in Git automatically configures the Project.

OWASP Excessive Agency requires minimum functionality, permissions and autonomy plus downstream authorization ([S22](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/)); NIST SSDF provides protected-development/change-control outcomes ([S23](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final)); SLSA specifies build provenance ([S24](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/requirements)). These standards bound the design but do not certify an agent or GitHub configuration.
primary_evidence: Ruleset composition and APIs: [S1](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets), [S2](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets), [S3](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules), [S17](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/orgs/rules); ruleset webhooks can trigger immediate drift inspection ([S19](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#repository_ruleset)).

Ownership/review semantics: [S4](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners) and [S5](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches). Key implication: owning `.github/CODEOWNERS`, workflows and policy files and requiring owner review is necessary, but eligible owners with bypass/write authority still need organizational separation.

Exact-head integration: merge queue behavior [S6](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue) and `merge_group` event [S7](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/events-that-trigger-workflows#merge_group); auto-merge UI and GraphQL mutation [S8](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/automatically-merging-a-pull-request), [S9](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#enablepullrequestautomerge). Auto-merge is scheduling, not risk acceptance.

Production protection: environment configuration/review and REST API [S10](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/manage-environments), [S11](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/review-deployments), [S28](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/deployments/environments). Environment secrets become available to the job only after rules pass; deploy only the reviewed immutable digest and separately verify artifact identity.

Identity and CI: GitHub App permissions [S15](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/choosing-permissions-for-a-github-app), Actions token permissions [S12](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication), security hardening/full-SHA pinning [S13](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions), OIDC [S26](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-hardening-your-deployments/about-security-hardening-with-openid-connect). Use separate App installations/identities for proposing, verifying, merging and deploying.

Audit/drift: audit log [S16](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/keeping-your-organization-secure/managing-security-settings-for-your-organization/managing-the-audit-log-for-your-organization), enterprise stream [S27](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/admin/monitoring-activity-in-your-enterprise/reviewing-audit-logs-for-your-enterprise/streaming-the-audit-log-for-your-enterprise), REST API conditional/idempotent practices [S30](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api), and rules troubleshooting [S31](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/troubleshooting-rules).
independent_evidence: GitHub Security Lab's 'Preventing pwn requests' shows how `pull_request_target` plus checkout/build of attacker-controlled PR code can yield repository write or secret compromise ([S14](https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/)). This challenges any policy that treats a green Actions run as independent without checking trigger, checkout SHA, token permissions and runner trust.

CISA's March 18, 2025 alert says `tj-actions/changed-files` was compromised and recommends locating uses, reviewing workflow output for leaked secrets, rotating secrets and updating to a safe version ([S20](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2025/03/18/supply-chain-compromise-third-party-tj-actionschanged-files-cve-2025-30066)). This is operational evidence that third-party CI actions are part of the trusted computing base; tag pinning alone is weaker than reviewed full-SHA pinning plus dependency monitoring.

A controlled study with 29 professionals and 72 reviews retained 89% of AI-surfaced issues, but the AI surfaced only 42% of 48 injected issues and showed no time saving ([S21](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.11401)). The sample is small and artificial, but it rejects 'AI review passed' as a substitute for required human/domain review.

OWASP warns excessive functionality, permissions and autonomy enable damaging agent actions and directs authorization to downstream systems rather than the LLM ([S22](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/)). GitHub CodeQL Autofix likewise says suggestions can be incorrect or introduce vulnerabilities and require review/testing ([S25](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/managing-code-scanning-alerts/responsible-use-autofix-code-scanning)).
metrics_and_limits: CODEOWNERS: GitHub documents a 3 MB file limit; over-limit files are not loaded, and `!` negation and escaping `#` are unsupported. Validate syntax/coverage in CI and split ownership by directory rather than generating an unreviewable file ([S4](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners)).

Environment required reviewers: up to six people or teams may be listed, but only one approval is required; 'prevent self-review' blocks the initiator, not all conflicts of interest ([S10](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/manage-environments)-[S11](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/review-deployments)). Encode two-person/high-risk approval in an external signed approval record or custom gate.

Ruleset status checks have an expected-source option; bind critical checks to the verifier GitHub App. Required checks accept successful/skipped/neutral outcomes according to GitHub semantics, so the policy job itself must fail closed rather than emit neutral/skipped for mandatory evidence ([S2](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets), [S5](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches)).

GitHub API use has primary/secondary rate limits and recommends serial requests, conditional requests, avoiding polling and exponential backoff ([S30](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)). Reconciliation must be event-driven plus periodic, checkpoint cursors/ETags, and pause rather than partially apply after rate-limit/abuse errors.

Independent review experiment: 29 professionals, 72 reviews, 48 injected issues, 42% surfaced, 89% of surfaced issues retained, no observed time saving ([S21](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.11401)). This is not a universal reviewer-catch rate.

Missing denominators: no representative public data establishes ruleset-bypass incidence, approval-rubber-stamp rate, merge-queue escape defects, Project/ruleset drift frequency, or current agent-caused production incidents. Measure locally by risk tier and policy version.
recommended_design: Adopt a deny-by-default R0-R4 policy. R0 analysis has no mutation. R1 low-risk reversible changes may become auto-merge eligible only after a pilot. R2 material behavior requires plan-owner and CODEOWNER PR approval plus staged release. R3 auth/IAM/crypto/data/destructive migration/CI-policy/infrastructure/package publishing requires specialist plan approval, independent two-person PR/exception approval and production release approval. R4 ambiguous, irreversible, no oracle/rollback, or self-governance is human-led/proposal-only.

Compute `effective_risk=max(ticket_declared, deterministic diff/path/dependency/capability detectors, runtime findings)`. The agent may recommend but never lower risk. Any edit to `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `.github/rulesets/**`, `.github/governance/**`, evaluator/hidden tests, deployment/IAM, lockfiles/new suppliers, migrations, public API, or telemetry/rollback controls raises the floor.

Separate principals: `proposal-app` can create/update its task branch and PR; `verifier` has read-only contents plus checks write and no branch write; `merge-controller` can enable auto-merge/queue only after signed policy decision; `deploy-controller` receives OIDC only after environment/external approval; human owners administer rules. No principal that authors a change may approve its plan, exception, PR or release.

Use GitHub-native rules as the last-mile enforcement but keep a deterministic control-plane ledger. Git is the reviewed desired configuration. The controller reads live rulesets/environments/App grants/ProjectV2, produces a plan, requires human approval for weakening/deletion or unexpected ownership changes, applies with API preconditions, reads back canonical state, and records desired hash/live hash/API response/audit event.

state_and_event_contract.approval_binding: Every decision token binds work_item_id, spec_revision/hash, PR number, exact head SHA, base SHA, risk tier, policy bundle hash, required evidence digest, approver stable identity/role, decision, timestamp and expiry. A head/base/policy/evidence change invalidates it; comments, labels and Project fields alone are not approval tokens.
state_and_event_contract.idempotency: Use delivery GUID + event type/resource ID as intake key; use `(work_item, head_sha, policy_hash, transition)` as decision key. Store raw webhook first, verify signature, apply compare-and-swap state transitions, use an outbox for API writes, and reread live state after ambiguous timeout.
state_and_event_contract.reconciliation: Webhooks accelerate but do not prove completeness. Periodically list live rulesets, environments, App grants and ProjectV2 fields/items; canonicalize unordered/default fields; compare with manifest. Safe additive/tightening drift can be proposed or auto-repaired only by pre-approved policy. Weakening, deletion, bypass additions, ownership changes and unknown objects block merges/deploys and page an owner. Project status is a projection: restore derived fields from ledger, but open a review for human-owned priority/intent conflicts.

repository_artifacts: `.github/CODEOWNERS` — explicit owners for application paths and self-owned control paths; CI tests every protected path and rejects unknown users/teams or an oversized/invalid file.

`.github/governance/risk-policy.v1.yaml`, `protected-paths.yaml`, `capability-profiles.yaml`, `merge-policy.yaml`, `deployment-policy.yaml` — JSON-Schema-validated enums, escalation predicates, check/App IDs, minimum approval roles/counts, rollback/expiry and no-bypass invariants.

`.github/rulesets/main.json`, `release-tags.json` and `environments/production.yaml` — normalized desired snapshots. They are inputs to a controller, not GitHub-native declarative state. Generated live snapshots belong under `audit/snapshots/` or an immutable store, never silently written by the proposal agent.

`.github/workflows/policy-check.yml`, `verify.yml`, `merge-group.yml`, `deploy.yml`, `drift-audit.yml` — minimal explicit permissions, full-SHA pinned actions, concurrency, timeouts, immutable artifact digest handoff. `merge-group.yml` handles `merge_group` and runs the same required check names.

`ops/reconcile-github.py` (or controller service), `ops/project-manifest.yaml`, `ops/github-app-permissions.yaml`, `runbooks/policy-drift.md`, `break-glass.md`, `merge-queue.md`, `production-rollback.md`. Store symbolic organization/team/project/field names plus stable aliases; resolve and persist remote IDs in controller state, not hand-edited manifests.
workflow_steps: 1. Intake authenticates webhook, stores raw event, reads the approved spec revision and computes risk from paths, semantic flags, dependencies, requested capabilities and rollback. Unknown classification stops at `PLAN_APPROVAL_REQUIRED`.

2. A human signs the exact plan/spec for R2/R3. The proposal App gets a short-lived branch-scoped token; it cannot edit protected control paths unless the task is explicitly governance-classed, in which case execution remains proposal-only.

3. Agent opens a draft PR with risk/evidence metadata. On every synchronize event, revoke prior decision tokens and rerun clean-room CI using read-only checkout and minimal token. Never build untrusted fork code under `pull_request_target` with secrets/write token ([S12](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication)-[S14](https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/)).

4. The verifier emits a signed evidence digest for the exact head. Policy checks required test/security/provenance results, protected-path ownership, approval roles/counts, unresolved conversations, exception validity and live-policy drift.

5. R1 proven task classes may become `AUTO_MERGE_ELIGIBLE`; merge-controller—not the author—enables auto-merge or queues the SHA. R2/R3 wait for qualified human approval. Merge queue reruns evidence on `merge_group`; missing, skipped unexpectedly, stale or wrong-App checks fail closed ([S5](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches)-[S9](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#enablepullrequestautomerge)).

6. After merge, build once and attest the immutable artifact. Release policy maps risk/environment. Production waits for an exact artifact+source+policy approval; environment approval unlocks OIDC, then canary/SLO checks promote or roll back ([S10](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/manage-environments)-[S11](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/review-deployments), [S24](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/requirements), [S26](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-hardening-your-deployments/about-security-hardening-with-openid-connect)).

7. Record final SHA/digest, approvals, checks, bypass/exception use, deployment and observation outcome. Reconciler continuously compares Git desired state with actual GitHub state. Close only after the observation window or explicit non-deployment disposition.
human_gates: R0: no execution approval because identity is read-only; require a human for consequential prioritization or publication. R1: human approves the task/spec during pilot; after measured promotion, no per-PR human is required only for a closed allowlisted class with independent checks, no protected paths/new dependencies, small bounded diff and easy rollback; random audits continue.

R2: product/technical owner approves the exact spec; at least one independent path-qualified CODEOWNER approves the exact head; release owner approves user-visible/production promotion. Scope or semantic change returns to planning.

R3: specialist approval before capability grant; two distinct qualified humans approve exact plan/PR/exception, including security/data/operations as applicable; production approval binds the exact artifact digest and rollout/rollback. Because GitHub environment reviewer lists require only one approval, implement the second signature outside that primitive ([S10](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/manage-environments)-[S11](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/review-deployments)).

R4: humans own the work. Agent can gather evidence/draft only. Always R4 for changes that grant itself merge/deploy/bypass/admin, alter its own policy/evaluator/hidden acceptance tests, delete audit evidence, or approve its own exception.

Exception/break-glass: human incident commander plus second approver where feasible; exact failed rule, SHA/digest, reason, scope, compensating controls, expiry, rollback and follow-up. Never waive audit integrity, secret disclosure response, identity separation, unknown artifact provenance or irreversible action without accountable human command.
security_and_failure_modes: Policy-as-text bypass: issue/comment/repository prompt injection convinces agent to relabel risk or edit gates. Mitigation: risk computed by signed deterministic policy outside model; control paths protected; agent has no rule administration/bypass/approval permission ([S22](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/)).

Check spoofing/staleness: same check name emitted by an untrusted workflow/App, green result for old SHA, skipped/neutral job, or missing `merge_group`. Mitigation: bind check to expected verifier App, SHA/base/policy/evidence digest; fail closed and test merge-group trigger ([S2](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets), [S5](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches)-[S7](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/events-that-trigger-workflows#merge_group)).

CI confused deputy: `pull_request_target`, untrusted checkout, cache/artifact poisoning, compromised action exposes write token/secrets. Mitigation: unprivileged PR workflow, separate privileged follow-up that consumes validated metadata only, explicit token permissions, no secrets, ephemeral runners, full-SHA actions and dependency monitoring ([S12](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication)-[S14](https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/), [S20](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2025/03/18/supply-chain-compromise-third-party-tj-actionschanged-files-cve-2025-30066)).

Ownership/bypass weakness: wildcard CODEOWNERS gap, invalid/oversize file, team loses write access, admin/ruleset bypass, deploy key bypass, actor approves own change. Mitigation: synthetic path coverage, live team membership checks, deny bypass by default, alert on ruleset/owner/App-grant event, separate administrators and quarterly access review ([S1](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets)-[S5](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches), [S19](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#repository_ruleset)).

TOCTOU/race: approval attaches to prior head/base/policy while merge queue tests another tree. Mitigation: cryptographic approval binding, stale dismissal, latest-push approval, queue revalidation and CAS transitions.

Remote drift/API partial failure: Git YAML says safe while live ruleset/environment/Project differs; webhook missed; rate limit leaves half-applied state. Mitigation: inventory remote IDs, canonical read-after-write, outbox/idempotency, periodic full scan, transaction plan with compensating rollback, `POLICY_DRIFT_BLOCKED` kill switch ([S3](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules), [S17](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/orgs/rules)-[S19](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#repository_ruleset), [S28](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/deployments/environments)-[S31](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/troubleshooting-rules)).

Rubber-stamp/AI review failure: green tests and an AI review miss semantics; controlled evidence found only 42% of injected issues surfaced ([S21](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.11401)). Use qualified human review for material/high risk, bounded diffs, semantic checklist and independent tests.

Deployment/exception abuse: environment admin bypass, one-of-six reviewer misunderstood as multi-party, expired exception remains active, mutable artifact rebuilt after review. Mitigation: external multi-signature gate, prevent self-review/admin bypass, TTL fail-close, promote exact attested digest, observe and automatically rollback.
validation_and_tests: Schema/property tests: all policy files parse; every change class maps to exactly one minimum risk; `effective_risk` never decreases when protected paths/capabilities/findings are added; missing/unknown fields deny; author cannot be an approver; expired approval/exception denies.

CODEOWNERS tests: enumerate repository paths and synthetic changed-file sets; ensure control/security/deploy paths have qualified owner teams; verify fork/base behavior assumptions; reject invalid syntax, 3 MB breach, missing write access and uncovered protected path ([S4](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners)).

Ruleset conformance tests: in a disposable organization/repository, apply manifests, read back canonical JSON and compare. Try direct push, force push, deletion, wrong-App status, skipped/neutral/missing check, stale approval, last-pusher self-approval, bypass actor and ruleset priority/composition. Snapshot both pass and deny audit events ([S1](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets)-[S5](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches), [S17](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/orgs/rules), [S19](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#repository_ruleset)).

Merge tests: PR update invalidates token; queue introduces base conflict/failing test; `merge_group` runs identical named checks; auto-merge cannot activate before policy decision; duplicate delivery/API retry performs one transition ([S6](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue)-[S9](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#enablepullrequestautomerge), [S30](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)).

Actions adversarial tests: fork PR edits scripts/action inputs, attempts `pull_request_target` secret exfiltration, cache/artifact substitution and dependency/action tag compromise. Assert token is read-only/no secrets and privileged stage never executes attacker code ([S12](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication)-[S14](https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/), [S20](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2025/03/18/supply-chain-compromise-third-party-tj-actionschanged-files-cve-2025-30066)).

Release chaos tests: self-review and admin bypass denied, wrong digest denied, OIDC audience/repository/environment mismatch denied, second signature required for R3, canary hard failure rolls back, inconclusive telemetry pauses and pages rather than promotes ([S10](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/manage-environments)-[S11](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/review-deployments), [S26](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-hardening-your-deployments/about-security-hardening-with-openid-connect)).

Reconciliation tests: delete/weaken live rule, add bypass, rename Project field, remove team access, miss webhook, inject 403/409/429/5xx/timeout. Assert drift blocks relevant transitions, safe retries do not duplicate, unknown remote object is quarantined, and weakening requires human-approved plan.
operational_maintenance: Continuously export GitHub audit plus controller append-only events; correlate delivery GUID, actor, work item, spec/head/base/policy hashes, checks, review IDs, exception, ruleset version, artifact digest and deployment. Protect the export separately; periodically test replay and gap detection ([S16](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/keeping-your-organization-secure/managing-security-settings-for-your-organization/managing-the-audit-log-for-your-organization), [S27](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/admin/monitoring-activity-in-your-enterprise/reviewing-audit-logs-for-your-enterprise/streaming-the-audit-log-for-your-enterprise)).

Run webhook-triggered reconciliation for ruleset/environment/team/App-grant changes and scheduled full reconciliation. Dashboard desired/live hash, last successful scan, unmanaged objects, bypass actors, CODEOWNERS coverage, stale approvals, active/expired exceptions, queue failures and environment bypasses.

Review App permissions, team membership and bypass lists monthly/quarterly based on consequence; rotate/revoke credentials; pin and update Actions through reviewed dependency PRs; verify attestation roots; test break-glass and known-good artifact/data rollback.

Measure by risk/policy version: proposal rejection, human review minutes, stale invalidations, auto-merge volume, queue failure, post-merge revert/escaped defect, deployment rollback/incident, exceptions count/age/recurrence, unauthorized attempts, drift detection and repair latency. Automatically suspend R1 auto-merge when preset error/incident/drift budgets breach.

Policy/self-improvement follows proposal -> offline policy fixtures/adversarial eval -> shadow decision comparison -> limited canary repository/task class -> independent governance approval -> versioned promotion -> rollback. The agent may author a proposal but cannot change baselines, hidden tests, thresholds, approver mapping or promotion decision.
maturity_and_uncertainty: Mature: GitHub CODEOWNERS, protected branches/rulesets, Actions checks, merge queue, environments, GitHub Apps and audit APIs are production controls with documented semantics. Conditional: their safe composition, because plans/features differ and configuration drift, bypass identities, CI trust and human behavior remain operator responsibilities.

Conditionally justified: unattended merge only for narrowly enumerated R1 classes after local shadow/pilot evidence, independent exact-head checks and rollback. Not justified: general agent self-merge, policy/permission self-change, high-risk production approval or irreversible action.

Experimental: treating Git repositories as declarative desired state for rulesets/environments/ProjectV2. APIs make a reconciler feasible, but GitHub does not provide a built-in transactional GitOps controller across these resources. Remote IDs, API evolution, rate limits, partial failure and human edits need explicit handling.

Overall confidence: HIGH on documented platform mechanics; MEDIUM on the recommended composition; LOW on quantitative residual risk because public bypass/incident/reviewer-effectiveness denominators are absent.
implementation_recommendation: Phase 0: protect main and control paths; install CODEOWNERS; create baseline ruleset with required expected-source policy/verify checks, stale approval dismissal, latest-push approval, conversation resolution, signed commits where feasible, restricted pushes and no routine bypass. Create separate proposal/verifier/merge/deploy Apps and explicit Actions permissions.

Phase 1: implement risk-policy schemas, approval/evidence/exception ledger, PR policy check and merge-group workflow. Require human PR/release approval for all changes. Add live snapshot/diff-only reconciler and alert on weakening.

Phase 2: apply controller-managed rulesets/environments in a sandbox then production with approved plan/read-after-write. Add ProjectV2 projection reconciliation while retaining ledger as truth. Pilot R1 docs/tests/allowlisted patch dependencies in shadow; compare would-merge to human results.

Phase 3: enable controller-owned auto-merge for proven R1 predicates only. Keep R2/R3 human gates. Add attested immutable artifact, OIDC environment release, canary/rollback, audit streaming and quarterly adversarial/permission drills.

Do not grant the coding agent admin, ruleset, environment, bypass, approval, merge, deployment, secret, package-publish or audit-delete authority. A self-improvement change uses the same R3 governed promotion path.

conflicts: Git-native policy versus actual enforcement: reviewed YAML is useful desired state, but GitHub rulesets, environment reviewers/App grants and ProjectV2 values are remote mutable resources. Resolution: never report 'compliant' from repository files alone; require live inventory, canonical diff, read-after-write and drift-blocking.

Rulesets can layer, while legacy branch protection applies only one matching rule ([S1](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets), [S5](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches)). Resolution: use rulesets for new enforcement and inventory legacy protection during migration; test the effective result, not assumed precedence.

CODEOWNERS looks like required review but is only routing until a branch/ruleset requires code-owner approval, and eligible owners need write access ([S4](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners)-[S5](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches)). Resolution: pair it with protected rules and independent identity/role checks; protect CODEOWNERS itself.

Environment UI can list six required reviewers, but only one listed reviewer must approve ([S10](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/manage-environments)-[S11](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/review-deployments)). Resolution: do not claim six-person or two-person approval; add an external/custom multi-signature gate for R3.

Auto-merge marketing language can sound autonomous, but GitHub defines it as merging after configured requirements pass ([S8](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/automatically-merging-a-pull-request)-[S9](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#enablepullrequestautomerge)). Resolution: a separate risk-policy controller decides eligibility; GitHub auto-merge is only the actuator.

A required status check may look trusted, but unsafe workflow triggers or a compromised Action can leak credentials or forge evidence ([S13](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions)-[S14](https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/), [S20](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2025/03/18/supply-chain-compromise-third-party-tj-actionschanged-files-cve-2025-30066)). Resolution: bind expected App, isolate untrusted code, pin Actions by full SHA, minimize token, and verify evidence provenance.

Human review is required for material risk, yet AI-assisted review can create automation bias and the small study found limited issue surfacing ([S21](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.11401)). Resolution: qualified independent humans, structured semantic review and executable independent evidence—not a generic approval click.

Audit logs are valuable but are provider records with plan-dependent coverage/retention, not the full workflow ledger ([S16](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/keeping-your-organization-secure/managing-security-settings-for-your-organization/managing-the-audit-log-for-your-organization), [S27](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/admin/monitoring-activity-in-your-enterprise/reviewing-audit-logs-for-your-enterprise/streaming-the-audit-log-for-your-enterprise)). Resolution: export promptly and keep a separate append-only signed controller ledger with gap detection.

confidence.overall: High for GitHub mechanism/API semantics; medium for the composed risk-tier design; low for quantitative residual loss and human-review effectiveness.
claim_level: High: CODEOWNERS, ruleset, protected branch, merge queue, environment, Actions token, App and audit behavior supported by official docs/schema ([S1](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets)-[S19](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#repository_ruleset), [S26](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-hardening-your-deployments/about-security-hardening-with-openid-connect)-[S31](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/troubleshooting-rules)).

Medium-high: CI supply-chain and privileged-trigger threats supported by GitHub Security Lab and CISA operational alert ([S14](https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/), [S20](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2025/03/18/supply-chain-compromise-third-party-tj-actionschanged-files-cve-2025-30066)).
Medium: human-review limitation from one small controlled study ([S21](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.11401)), not a universal production rate.
Medium: exact R0-R4 boundaries and approval counts are engineering recommendations based on consequence and separation of duties, not a GitHub standard or controlled trial.
Low: frequency of remote drift, bypass abuse, agent incidents and benefit/cost of R1 auto-merge absent repository-specific longitudinal data.

uncertain: The as-of date is future-facing relative to many fixed publications. GitHub living documentation often has no visible update date and features vary by GitHub plan, repository visibility, Enterprise Cloud/Server version and policy; verify against the target tenant before rollout.

No official cross-resource transaction or native repository-to-ruleset/environment/ProjectV2 GitOps reconciliation contract was found. The proposed reconciler is an implementation design built from available APIs/webhooks, with unavoidable eventual consistency and partial-failure handling.
Exact API preview/version details, ruleset rule availability and custom deployment protection capabilities may change. Pin the GitHub API version, use schema/contract tests and stage upgrades.

No public representative measurement was found for current agent PR defect escape after merge queues, ruleset bypass frequency, approval fatigue, environment bypass, live configuration drift or agent-triggered production incidents.

Two-person R3 approval needs a custom/external binding because native environment required-reviewer lists use one-of semantics. The precise custom protection-rule availability and licensing must be checked for the organization.

Risk tiers, protected-path triggers, diff ceilings, observation windows and error budgets must be calibrated from local history; the proposed defaults are governance architecture, not empirically universal thresholds.
